Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
docs(Common): Replace literal em spaces with HTML numeric entity in markdown

GitHub-flavored Markdown handles literal Unicode em spaces (U+2001) inconsistently across browsers and renderers, causing visual alignment breakage in headers, table cells, and diagram labels. Replace all `\u2001` characters with the ` ` HTML numeric entity, which renders reliably in every context.

Changes span all three documentation files:
- `README.md` — Em spaces in section headings, tables, connection path diagrams, and emblem grid condensed to single-line `<td>` elements
- `Documentation/GitHub/Architecture.md` — Same treatment across all section headers and table cells
- `Documentation/GitHub/DeepDive.md` — Consistent enitization for all em-space-delimited headings and component references

Additionally, condense the multi-line `<td>` sponsor grid in README.md to single-line markup for consistency with the rest of the file. All rendered HTML tables and section headings now display with correct spacing across GitHub, VS Code preview, and standalone renderers.

docs(Common): Revise README for accessibility and clarity

Rewrite the Common crate README to improve readability for newcomers unfamiliar with the project architecture. Replace the dense, formal prose with plain-language explanations, emoji anchors for sibling components, and shorter paragraphs organized around the crate's six key abstractions (service traits, ActionEffect system, DTOs, CommonError, transport layer, telemetry).

Update the badge label for the last-commit badge from "Last-commit" to "Update" for brevity, rename the issues badge label from "Issues" to "Issue", change the downloads badge label from "Downloads" to "Download", and fix the downloads URL path to include the "/total" suffix so the badge resolves correctly.

The revised README better serves both new contributors and project maintainers by emphasizing the architectural rationale (why abstractions exist) and the testing benefits of the design.

Message:
feat(Common): Add editor Sky events and call/type hierarchy prep

Extend the IPC surface in SkyEvent.rs with five new editor-related event URIs used by Mountain→Sky communication for text editor interaction:

- DecorationSetRanges ("sky://decoration/set-ranges") — fired when an extension calls setDecorations, enabling Monaco decoration rendering via ICodeEditorService
- EditorApplyTextEdits ("sky://editor/apply-text-edits") — payload channel for editor.edit() calls with range+text edits
- EditorSelectionChanged ("sky://editor/selection-changed") — forwards selection changes from Sky to Cocoon via window.didChangeTextEditorSelection
- EditorActiveChanged ("sky://editor/active-changed") — fires when a text editor tab is activated, passing uri, viewColumn, selections
- EditorRevealRange ("sky://editor/revealRange") — scrolls Monaco to a specific range with a reveal type

Add PrepareCallHierarchy and PrepareTypeHierarchy as required entry-point methods on the LanguageFeatureProviderRegistry trait. These sit alongside the existing ProvideTypeHierarchySupertypes/Subtypes methods, completing the hierarchy provider lifecycle — Mountain must call Prepare before requesting incoming/outgoing calls, matching the VS Code LanguageFeatureRequest pattern.

Both additions close gaps identified during Wind/Cocoon integration of editor decorations and call/type hierarchy features.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(common): Add Storage, Workspace, Language, SCM, Debug, Task, and Auth IPC channels

Expanded the IPC channel definitions in `Channel.rs` to cover multiple missing service domains required for full VS Code API parity.

Added the following new channel groups:
- Storage: Introduced `StorageOnDidChangeItems` (event stub) and `StorageLogStorage`.
- Workspaces: Added event stubs for folder/name changes (`WorkspacesOnDidChangeWorkspaceFolders`, `WorkspacesOnDidChangeWorkspaceName`) and CRUD methods for workspace configurations (`GetWorkspace`, `GetWorkspaceFolders`, `Add/RemoveWorkspaceFolders`).
- Languages: Defined `LanguagesGetAll` and `LanguagesGetEncodedLanguageId` to support language identification queries via the NodeDeferred path.
- SCM: Added core Source Control Management operations including `CreateSourceControl`, `GetSourceControls`, and `SetActiveProvider`.
- Debug: Implemented full lifecycle and state management channels (`Start/StopDebugging`, `GetSessions`, `Get/Add/RemoveBreakpoints`).
- Tasks: Added execution and retrieval channels (`ExecuteTask`, `GetTasks`, `GetTaskExecution`).
- Authentication: Introduced session management channels (`GetSessions`, `CreateSession`, `RemoveSession`).

Additionally, updated the `ChannelPriority` implementation to classify the new Storage and Workspace event channels as `Low` priority, aligning them with other asynchronous telemetry or event-driven traffic. These additions ensure the IPC registry recognizes these routes, preventing "Unknown channel" errors while allowing the Tauri/NodeDeferred layer to handle dispatch logic.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Common): Add W3C traceparent builder for cross-tier distributed tracing

Extend the `Telemetry` module in Common with a new `Traceparent` component to standardize distributed context propagation across tier boundaries (Mountain ↔ Cocoon, Mountain ↔ Sky, Sidecars). Implement `Build` and `Parse` functions for W3C version-00 `traceparent` headers, ensuring every process maintains a stable `TraceId` while minting unique `SpanId` values for each inter-process call.

This addition unifies the observability surface by allowing OTLP and PostHog events to share a consistent trace identity, enabling end-to-end tracing from the editor UI through the native backend and into the extension host. The implementation derives the trace ID deterministically from the process ID and current nanosecond timestamp to ensure agreement between the OTLP exporter and the header builder, even across separate modules.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Common): Introduce shared dual-pipe telemetry module for sidecars

Add a new `Telemetry` module to the Common crate to standardize observability across all Rust sidecars (Air, Echo, Rest, Grove, Mist) and the Mountain backend. This module implements a dual-pipe architecture supporting both PostHog for product analytics and OTLP for distributed tracing.

The implementation provides a runtime-configured client initialized once per process via `Initialize::Fn`, which stamps every event with the specific `Tier` (e.g., 'air', 'echo') and standard Land identity properties. It includes helper functions for capturing events (`CaptureEvent`), errors (`CaptureError`), and session starts (`CaptureSession`), alongside a fire-and-forget OTLP span exporter (`EmitOTLPSpan`).

Key architectural decisions include:
- `cfg!(debug_assertions)` gating to completely strip telemetry logic from release builds.
- Runtime configuration via environment variables for PostHog and OTLP endpoints.
- Atomic caching of configuration and a `OnceLock` singleton for the PostHog client to minimize boot overhead.
- Stable distinct ID generation to unify user sessions across multiple sidecar processes.

This change unifies the telemetry surface, replacing ad-hoc logging with a robust, dashboard-ready pipeline for the Errors & Reliability and Boot & Startup Performance dashboards.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Common): Add SkyEvent registry for Mountain → Wind Tauri events

Mountain emits Tauri events on `sky://…` URIs to notify the webview of
state changes that don't originate from a Wind-initiated `invoke` call.
Historically each emit site used a free-text string literal and each Wind
listener matched against its own free-text string — drift was invisible
until runtime (the listener simply never fired).

`SkyEvent` provides the single source of truth, following the same
`DefineSkyEvents!` macro pattern established for `Channel`. The enum
produces wire strings via `AsStr()` and parses them via `FromStr`, with
~100 events covering Configuration, Debug, Diagnostics, Dialog, Documents,
Editor, Extensions, ExtHost, Input, Language, Lifecycle, Native,
Notifications, Output, Progress, QuickPick, SCM, Status bar, Task, Terminal,
Test, Theme, Tree view, UI, VFS, Webview, Window, and Workspace.

This change also adds 3 legacy channels to Channel.rs that predate the
`prefix:method` convention: `MountainGetStatus` (snake_case) and the
`UserInterface.Show*Dialog` dotted names from the original Cocoon→Mountain
gRPC protocol.

The matching TypeScript const object lives at Element/Wind/Source/IPC/SkyEvent.ts,
kept in sync by convention. This eliminates silent runtime failures from typos
in event names and enables compile-time verification of the event namespace.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Common): Add QuickInput, TextFile, and WorkingCopy IPC channels

Extend the IPC Channel registry with 9 new channel definitions across three categories needed for Wind ↔ Mountain communication:

- QuickInput: showInputBox and showQuickPick for VS Code-style dialogs
- TextFile: read, write, and save operations for the editor's working-copy surface
- WorkingCopy: getAllDirty, getDirtyCount, isDirty, and setDirty for dirty-state tracking

These channels complete the IPC contract for the text editor and quick input services, enabling the Wind frontend to invoke these backend operations via Tauri invoke calls.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Common): Add centralized IPC Channel registry for Wind ↔ Mountain

Add a new Channel module in Common that enumerates all 147 IPC channel
identifiers used in Tauri invoke calls between Wind (TypeScript UI) and
Mountain (Rust backend). Previously these string identifiers were hand-kept
on both sides, causing drift where channels could be declared but lack
implementations.

The DefineChannels! macro generates the enum, AsStr(), All(), and FromStr
implementations from a single declarative list. The matching TypeScript
const object lives at Element/Wind/Source/IPC/Channel.ts, kept in sync
by convention.

This provides a single source of truth for the IPC channel namespace,
eliminating the possibility of runtime "unknown channel" errors from
typos or missing implementations.
